findings.evidence: "the consortium's circulation team reviews monthly checkout volume after each fiscal period" vs. "the consortium's circulation team audits monthly checkout volume on the first of every month"
findings.fix: State a single, specific review cadence, or clarify how the two described processes relate to each other.
findings.violation: These two statements describe different, seemingly incompatible review cadences (after each fiscal period vs. monthly on the first) without reconciling them.

findings.evidence: "It seems that the consortium's circulation team reviews monthly checkout volume..." / "...any branch that misses a reporting deadline is flagged for follow-up the next week."
findings.fix: Remove this section or explain explicitly how circulation reporting practices bear on the overdue-fines decision.
findings.violation: This entire section about reporting cadence and archiving is never connected to the fines recommendation and is not referenced anywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Ending overdue fines is plainly the better path for the consortium, and delaying the change would only cost every branch more."
findings.fix: Move the conclusion after the evidence, and remove or substantiate the unsupported "every branch" cost claim.
findings.violation: This is a flat conclusion asserted before any supporting evidence is presented, and it claims a cost to "every branch" even though the pilot covered only four of ten branches.

findings.evidence: "self-reported avoidance of the library due to fear of fines dropped from 20 percent of respondents before the pilot to 3 percent after it" vs. "the survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot"
findings.fix: Use consistent, precise language for when the second survey occurred (e.g., "twelve months after the pilot began" vs. "at the pilot's conclusion") and ensure both sentences agree.
findings.violation: The first sentence says the second survey was taken "after" the pilot, while the second sentence says it was taken "twelve months into the pilot," which may not be the same point in time if the pilot ran longer than twelve months.

findings.evidence: Section heading is "What the Pilot Showed," but only the avoidance-survey finding is reported; no return-rate figures appear anywhere in this section.
findings.fix: Add the actual return-rate figures from the pilot here, or remove references to "return-rate results" elsewhere in the document.
findings.location: "What the Pilot Showed" (section as a whole)
findings.violation: Later sections repeatedly cite "return-rate ... results" from the pilot (e.g., in "Recommendation" and "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide"), but no return-rate data is ever actually presented.

findings.evidence: "Given the return-rate and avoidance-survey results above, the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches"
findings.fix: Either present the return-rate data earlier or remove this unsupported reference.
findings.violation: This cites "return-rate" results as a basis for the recommendation, but no such results were presented above.

findings.evidence: "Specifically, the recommended change is about making things better for patrons going forward, in whatever way the consortium finds workable."
findings.fix: Replace with a specific description of the policy change, or delete the sentence.
findings.violation: The sentence is introduced with "Specifically" but is entirely vague and provides no concrete content, contradicting its own framing.

findings.evidence: "This recommendation removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification."
findings.fix: Scope the recommendation to what the evidence actually supports, or explicitly justify the unqualified, permanent, all-items claim.
findings.violation: The absolute scope ("permanently," "every item," "without qualification") is not supported by the pilot data, which covered only four branches over a limited period and did not test all item types.

findings.evidence: "this relationship ... is the reason the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results, taken together, support ending fines for the whole consortium rather than only the pilot branches"
findings.fix: Supply the missing return-rate data and explicitly argue why the untested branches should be expected to respond similarly to the pilot branches.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide," first paragraph
findings.violation: Again invokes "return-rate" results never shown, and asserts without argument that results from 4 of 10 branches justify extending the policy to the other 6 untested branches.

findings.evidence: "removing the financial penalty for late returns predictably increases both on-time return rates and overall program participation"
findings.fix: Define "program participation," cite the data supporting the claimed increase, or remove the claim.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide," first paragraph
findings.violation: "Overall program participation" is introduced here for the first time with no prior data or definition; it was never measured or mentioned in the pilot description.

findings.evidence: "documented in the Tri-County Library Data Cooperative's 2023 fines-elimination research brief, which reviewed return-rate data from fourteen library systems"
findings.fix: Explain why the cited systems are comparable to the consortium's branches, or rely on the consortium's own data instead.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide," second paragraph
findings.violation: An external study of fourteen unrelated library systems is used to generalize the consortium's own four-branch pilot to all ten branches, without addressing whether those systems are comparable to the consortium.

findings.evidence: "This tends to hold: a skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding, and argues that eliminating them systemwide will leave a shortfall..."
findings.fix: Rephrase to neutrally present the objection (e.g., "A skeptic argues...") without prejudging its validity before the rebuttal.
findings.violation: "This tends to hold" frames the skeptic's objection as generally valid, which contradicts the following paragraph's rebuttal that the shortfall "has not materialized."

findings.evidence: "It might be that consortium finance records show fine revenue covered under 2 percent of the annual materials budget over the last three fiscal years"
findings.fix: State the finance-records figure as a confirmed fact with a specific percentage, not a hedged guess.
findings.violation: A hedge ("It might be") is applied to what is presented as a factual record lookup, undermining the reliability of the key rebuttal evidence, and "under 2 percent" is vague compared to the precise figures used elsewhere (20 percent, 3 percent).
